## Investment {#sec-pw-investment}

Investment fills the capacity needed with new plants. The cheapest types by levelised cost take most of it, but
no type can grow faster than its scale-up limit, and only types the scenario permits are built. What the first,
cost-weighted round cannot place goes, in a second round, to the cheapest types with room left.

The methodology describes this in
[section 3.4.2.4.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#investment-decision-and-non-vre-and-vre-scale-up-limitations).

### Investment permitted and scale-up limits {#sec-pw-scaleup}

A type can be built in year $t$ when the scenario permits it and $t$ has reached its first year of investment
($\zeta_{f,t}$, [Inputs of the scenario](#sec-pw-a0)). The options of `NewInv<type>` are:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| If Present* (default) | Permitted if the type has more than 0.1% of base-year capacity |
| Yes | Permitted from the year `NewInv<type>Year` |
| No | Never built |
| Manual | Built along a capacity path typed by the user ([Manual capacity](#sec-pw-manual)); no logit investment |

The scale-up limit caps each type's new effective capacity at a share of total effective capacity:

$$
iv^{max}_{f,t} = q_f\, \zeta_{f,t} \sum_j cap^e_{j,t}
$$ {#eq-pw-maxinv}

where $iv^{max}_{f,t}$ is the maximum effective investment (MW; `maxinv`) and $q_f$ the scale-up rate: 5% of total
for coal, gas and hydro, 2% for oil, nuclear, other renewables and biomass, and the wind and solar rate of the
scenario (country default 2%) ([Inputs of the scenario](#sec-pw-a0)). The limit is linear: it is a share of the
system's total, in gross additions, not net of retirements.

### First round: the logit {#sec-pw-first-round}

The need, net of any manual investment, is shared among the permitted types by a logit on levelised investment costs
relative to the cheapest permitted type:

$$
\lambda^{i}_{f,t} = \frac{\zeta_{f,t}\, e^{-K_i\, tic_{f,t}/tic^{lc}_t}}{\sum_j \zeta_{j,t}\, e^{-K_i\, tic_{j,t}/tic^{lc}_t}},
\qquad
tic^{lc}_t = \max\left(\min_{j:\ \zeta_{j,t} = 1} tic_{j,t},\ c_{min}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-lgi}

$$
inv^{(1)}_{f,t} = \min\left(iv^{max}_{f,t},\ need^m_t\, \lambda^i_{f,t}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-first}

where

- $\lambda^i_{f,t}$ is the investment share of type $f$ (`pni`; its weight is `lgi`);
- $tic^{lc}_t$ the lowest levelised investment cost of the permitted types (`cmin`);
- $K_i$ = `kInvestment` (default 2);
- $need^m_t$ the need net of manual investment (@eq-pw-needm);
- $inv^{(1)}_{f,t}$ new effective investment of the first round (MW; `first`).

This is the methodology's $ivp_f/\sum ivp = \zeta_f\, e^{-K_i H_i}/\sum e^{-K_i H_i}$ with
$H_i = tic/tic^{lc}$, and the equation list's ([M4.6](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M4-6)).

### Second round: cheapest first {#sec-pw-second-round}

What the scale-up limits leave unplaced is the deficit. It goes to the types with space left under their limits,
cheapest first, each taking as much as its space allows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
deficit_t &= \max\left(need^m_t - \sum_f inv^{(1)}_{f,t},\ 0\right) \\
space_{f,t} &= \left(iv^{max}_{f,t} - inv^{(1)}_{f,t}\right) \zeta_{f,t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-deficit}

$$
\begin{aligned}
inv^{(2)}_{f,t} &= \zeta_{f,t}\, \max\left(0,\ \min\left(space_{f,t},\ deficit_t - S_{f,t}\right)\right) \\
S_{f,t} &= \sum_{j:\ tic_{j,t} + tb_j\, <\, tic_{f,t} + tb_f} space_{j,t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-second}

where

- $deficit_t$ is investment left for the second round (MW; `deficit`);
- $space_{f,t}$ the remaining space under the scale-up limit (MW; `space`);
- $S_{f,t}$ the space of all cheaper types;
- $tb_f$ a tie breaker, $1.356 \times 10^{-6}$ USD/kWh times the type's position minus one (coal 0, ..., biomass 8),
  so that two types of equal cost are ranked in the type order (`TieBreak`);
- $inv^{(2)}_{f,t}$ new effective investment of the second round (MW; `second`).

A type takes what is left of the deficit after all cheaper types have filled their space.

### Final deficit to gas {#sec-pw-deficit-gas}

If even the second round cannot place the whole need (all permitted types at their limits), the rest is unplaced,
unless the global setting `PwDeficitGas` is Yes (default No). Then it goes to gas:

$$
d^{gas}_t = \mathbb{1}[\texttt{PwDeficitGas} = \text{Yes}] \left(deficit_t - \sum_f inv^{(2)}_{f,t}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-dgas}

(MW; `dgas`).

### Manual capacity and investment {#sec-pw-manual}

Where a scenario sets `NewInv<type>` = Manual, the type follows a capacity path typed by the user on the sheet
'Manual inputs' (one block for scenario 1, one for the other scenarios). It gets no logit investment (its permit is 0),
and its investment replaces next year's increase in the path plus this year's retirement:

$$
inv^{m}_{f,t} = \max\left(0,\ cap^{man}_{f,t+1} - cap^{man}_{f,t} + ret_{f,t}\right) cf_f, \qquad inv^m_{f,T} = 0
$$ {#eq-pw-mani}

$$
need^m_t = \max\left(need_t - \sum_f inv^m_{f,t},\ 0\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-needm}

where $cap^{man}_{f,t}$ is the manual capacity path (MW; `mancap`; blank = 0), $inv^m_{f,t}$ manual new effective
investment (MW; `mani`) and $need^m_t$ the need left for the logit and second rounds (`needm`). The methodology
describes the option as "New Nameplate Investments = Capacity data entered by the user + Planned Retirement".

### New investment, its cost and its share in the stock {#sec-pw-nim}

New effective investment sums the rounds; nameplate investment divides by the capacity factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
inv^e_{f,t} &= inv^{(1)}_{f,t} + inv^{(2)}_{f,t} + \mathbb{1}[f = \text{gas}]\; d^{gas}_t + inv^m_{f,t} \\
inv_{f,t} &= inv^e_{f,t}/cf_f
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-nim}

The spending and the share of new plants in next year's stock follow:

$$
Inv^{USD}_{f,t} = \frac{inv_{f,t}\, cax_{f,t}}{1000},
\qquad
\Phi_{f,t} = \frac{inv_{f,t}}{cap_{f,t} + inv_{f,t} - ret_{f,t}}
$$ {#eq-pw-phi}

where

- $inv^e_{f,t}$ is new effective investment (MW; `nei`) and $inv_{f,t}$ new nameplate investment (MW; `nim`), which
  becomes capacity in $t+1$ (@eq-pw-cap);
- $Inv^{USD}_{f,t}$ investment spending (USD million; `nid`) at the capital cost of the year;
- $\Phi_{f,t}$ new investment as a share of the stock after retirements (`phi`), used by the vintage averages of
  $t+1$ (@eq-pw-caxav).

Totals over types are `nimtot` and `usdtot`. The equation list has the second round in
([A4.9](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-9)).

### PPAs and investment {#sec-pw-ppa-investment}

PPAs do not enter the investment rounds directly. They act on the year's dispatch (@eq-pw-gen) and keep coal plants
from retiring early (@eq-pw-early); the PPA share $\omega_t$ is defined in @eq-pw-ppa.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: investment"}
```
for t in years:
    for f in types:
        mancap[f,t] = manual_path[f,t] if any else 0
        mani[f,t]   = (max(0, mancap[f,t+1] - mancap[f,t] + ret[f,t]) * cfu[f]
                       if invs[f] == 'Manual' and t < 2041 else 0)
    needm[t] = max(need[t] - sum(mani[f,t] for f in types), 0)
    cmin[t]  = max(min(tic[f,t] for f in types if permit[f,t] == 1), MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice)
    for f in types:
        lgi[f,t] = permit[f,t] * exp(-kInvestment * tic[f,t] / cmin[t])
    for f in types:
        pni[f,t]   = lgi[f,t] / sum(lgi[j,t] for j in types)
        first[f,t] = min(maxinv[f,t], needm[t] * pni[f,t])
    deficit[t] = max(needm[t] - sum(first[f,t] for f in types), 0)
    for f in types:
        space[f,t] = (maxinv[f,t] - first[f,t]) * permit[f,t]
    for f in types:
        cheaper     = sum(space[j,t] for j in types if tic[j,t] + tb[j] < tic[f,t] + tb[f])
        second[f,t] = permit[f,t] * max(0, min(space[f,t], deficit[t] - cheaper))
    dgas[t] = deficit[t] - sum(second[f,t] for f in types) if PwDeficitGas == 'Yes' else 0
    for f in types:
        nei[f,t] = first[f,t] + second[f,t] + (dgas[t] if f == 'nga' else 0) + mani[f,t]
        nim[f,t] = nei[f,t] / cfu[f]
        nid[f,t] = nim[f,t] * cax[f,t] / 1000                          # USD million
        phi[f,t] = nim[f,t] / (cap[f,t] + nim[f,t] - ret[f,t])
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 3, sub-table L: rows `mancap`, `mani`, `needm`, `cmin`, `deficit`, `permit`,
  `maxinv`, `lgi`, `pni`, `first`, `space`, `second`, `dgas`, `nei`, `nim`, `nimtot`, `nid`, `usdtot`, `phi`
  (Formulas.md E420-E438; LAMBDAs `FIRSTROUND`, `CHEAPFILL`). Manual capacity on 'Manual inputs' rows 349-357
  (scenario 1) and 363-371 (other scenarios), names `ManCapVal`, `ManCapYr`; scenario inputs `NewInv<type>`,
  `NewInv<type>Year`, `kInvestment`; Settings C45 `PwDeficitGas`; constant `TieBreak`.
- **CPAT Python:** `power.step()`, block "retirement and investment" (EQ-M4.6, EQ-A4.9). The manual capacity rows
  `mancap` and `mani` are set to 0: the 'Manual inputs' capacity block is empty in the data, and CPAT Python does not
  read a manual capacity path.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: investment"}
- **L6 (fixed).** Legacy normalises the investment logit by the cheapest type including types that may not be built
  (row 4046); the model by the cheapest permitted type.
- **L5 (fixed).** Legacy values investment spending at the capital cost at time factor 1; the model at the capital
  cost of the year (rows 4276-4284).
- **L12 (fixed).** Legacy's total nameplate investment row is zero; the model sums the types.
- **L118 (fixed).** Legacy computes the need net of manual investment (row 4108) but never uses it, so its logit
  investment comes on top of the manual one. The model sizes the logit and second-round investment on the net need.
- **Second round.** Legacy uses rows 4169-4246 (L11-L17); the model computes it in one row per type with the tie
  breaker.
- **Deficit to gas (LD78, issue I57).** A global setting (Settings C45), as legacy's typed switch E4248 (No), row 4252.
- **Methodology.** The methodology caps investment at total *generation* times the rate; the model, as legacy, at
  total *effective capacity* times the rate. The methodology says that, *in extremis*, the model overrides the VRE
  limits and the permitted types and invests in proportion to current capacity; the model does not: an unplaced
  deficit stays unplaced unless `PwDeficitGas` sends it to gas. The methodology quotes the CountrySpecific VRE rate as
  2% except China 2.5%; the data give 3% for China and India.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: results for Egypt"}
Egypt permits gas, oil, wind, solar and hydro (hydro from 2030); coal, nuclear, other renewables and biomass are not
present and so not permitted. Data edition Public01:

| New nameplate investment (MW) | 2022 | 2023 | 2026 | 2030 | 2035 | 2041 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gas, scenario 1 | 506 | 0 | 3,706 | 1,104 | 3,657 | 3,965 |
| Gas, scenario 2 | 467 | 0 | 3,706 | 1,342 | 3,659 | 3,798 |
| Wind, scenario 1 | 728 | 0 | 1,346 | 1,652 | 2,217 | 2,889 |
| Solar, scenario 1 | 800 | 0 | 1,697 | 2,296 | 2,793 | 3,641 |
| Hydro, scenario 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 414 | 717 | 754 |

- Solar's first-round investment equals its scale-up limit in most years (2026: 546 effective MW): the logit wants
  more solar than the limit allows. Wind and gas are also at their limits (gas: 5% of total effective capacity,
  1,365 effective MW). Of the deficit of 4,312 effective MW in 2026, the second round places 517 MW (oil, the only
  type with space left); the rest stays unplaced (`PwDeficitGas` = No). Dispatch absorbs the shortfall: gas runs
  above its base-year capacity factor, up to its maximum of 0.9.
- In 2023 the demand shock leaves no need, so nothing is built.
- Scenario test (manual capacity, scenario 2, nuclear 2,400 MW from 2030): 2,400 MW nameplate is built in 2029, then
  the retirements are replaced.
- Final deficit to gas: tested with tight scale-up limits; the workbook matches the Python reference.
:::

## Systems integration cost of renewables: storage {#sec-pw-storage}

The model has no hourly profiles, so it cannot see when wind and solar fall short. Instead it charges variable
renewables a systems integration cost that rises with their share of generation: the cost of the storage the system
needs at the margin. Short-term storage (batteries) is needed at any share; long-term storage (electrolysers and
hydrogen tanks) only above a threshold, and it is costly.

The methodology describes this in
[section 3.4.2.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-StorageDecision): short-term storage in
[3.4.2.5.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#short-term-storage), long-term storage in
[3.4.2.5.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#long-term-storage), and its levelised cost in
[3.4.2.5.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#levelized-cost-of-storage).

### VRE share {#sec-pw-vre}

$$
v_t = \sum_f \ell_f\, s_{f,t} = s_{wnd,t} + s_{sol,t} + s_{ore,t}
$$ {#eq-pw-vre}

(`vre`): the share of wind, solar and other renewables in generation of the year, from dispatch. Hydro and biomass
are not variable renewables.

### Short-term storage {#sec-pw-storage-short}

Total short-term storage is a quadratic function of the VRE share, $sst = h_{100}\, v^2$ hours of storage per kW of
average generation, with $h_{100}$ = 9 hours for a 100% VRE system. The marginal need is its derivative,
$d\,sst/dv = 2\, h_{100}\, v = 18\, v$ ([corrections, DOC6](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/08_Corrections.html#corrections-of-2026-10-31)).
A share $a_{st}$ of it is allocated to the power system. The cost of one marginal hour per kWh is

$$
c^{ph}_t = \frac{c^{bat}_t + c^{int}_t / r_{st}}{dlf_{ren}\, H} + \frac{o^{bat}_t}{H}
$$ {#eq-pw-cph}

where

- $c^{ph}_t$ is the short-term storage cost per marginal hour (USD/kWh; `cph`);
- $c^{bat}_t$ the battery capital cost (USD/kWh of storage), $c^{int}_t$ the battery interface capital cost (USD/kW),
  $o^{bat}_t$ the battery fixed operating cost (USD/kWh/year) ([Year paths](#sec-pw-data-paths));
- $r_{st}$ = `StorageToInterfaceRatioSTStorage` (default 2 hours): kWh of storage per kW of interface, a low,
  conservative ratio;
- $dlf_{ren}$ the discounted lifetime of renewables (average of wind and solar).

### Long-term storage {#sec-pw-storage-long}

Long-term storage is measured by its interface, the electrolysers (kW per kW of average generation). It is zero below
a VRE share $x$ and rises quadratically to $u_{lt}$ at 100% VRE:

$$
slt = u_{lt}\left(\frac{\max(0,\ v - x)}{1 - x}\right)^2,
\qquad
\frac{d\,slt}{dv} = u_{lt}\, \frac{2 \max(0,\ v - x)}{(1 - x)^2}
$$ {#eq-pw-slt}

where $x$ = `StartingPointWhenLTStorageIsNeeded` (default 0.75) and $u_{lt}$ = `LongTermStorageFor100pcVRE`
(default 1). With the defaults the marginal units needed are:

| VRE share $v$ | 75% or less | 85% | 90% | 95% | 100% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marginal kW of electrolysers per kW | 0 | 3.2 | 4.8 | 6.4 | 8.0 |

([corrections, DOC7](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/08_Corrections.html#corrections-of-2026-10-31)). The cost of one
marginal unit is

$$
c^{el}_t = \frac{c^{elx}_t + c^{tank}_t\, h_{lt}}{dlf_{ren}\, H} + \frac{o^{el}_t}{H} + v^{el}_t
$$ {#eq-pw-cel}

where

- $c^{el}_t$ is the long-term storage cost per marginal unit (USD/kWh; `cel`);
- $c^{elx}_t$ the electrolyser capital cost (USD/kW), $c^{tank}_t$ the storage tank capital cost (USD/kWh),
  $o^{el}_t$ the electrolyser fixed opex (USD/kW/year), $v^{el}_t$ its variable opex (USD/kWh);
- $h_{lt}$ = `StorageHoursForLTStorage` (default 1,000 hours of storage per kW).

### Marginal storage cost {#sec-pw-msc}

The marginal storage cost of variable renewables adds the two:

$$
msc_t = a_{st}\, 2\, h_{100}\, v_t\; c^{ph}_t
+ \frac{2 \max(0,\ v_t - x)}{(1 - x)^2}\; c^{el}_t\; a_{lt}\, u_{lt}
$$ {#eq-pw-msc}

where

- $msc_t$ is the marginal storage cost (USD/kWh; `msc`), charged to wind, solar and other renewables, 0 for the other
  types;
- $a_{st}$ = `AllocateSTStorageToVRE` (default 1) and $h_{100}$ = `TotalHoursStorageFor100pcVRE` (default 9); their
  product with 2 is the row `stm`;
- $a_{lt}$ = `AllocateLTStorageToVRE` (default 0.33), the share of long-term storage allocated to the power system
  (batteries and hydrogen have other uses); $a_{lt} u_{lt}$ is the row `ltu`.

The marginal storage cost enters the cost of renewables in two places: the vintage storage cost of the existing stock
(@eq-pw-stoav), which reaches the average generation cost and prices, and the levelised fixed cost of new plants
(@eq-pw-lfx), which drives investment. The storage-inclusive cost of renewables can therefore rise over time as their
share grows, even while their capital cost falls. The system is assumed to have invested optimally in the storage of
the current VRE share.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: storage"}
```
# before the year loop
for t in years:
    dlfr     = (dlf['wnd'] + dlf['sol']) / 2
    cph[t]   = (cbat[t] + cint[t] / StorageToInterfaceRatioSTStorage) / (dlfr * 8760) + obat[t] / 8760
    cel[t]   = (elcx[t] + eltk[t] * StorageHoursForLTStorage) / (dlfr * 8760) + elof[t] / 8760 + elov[t]
    stm      = AllocateSTStorageToVRE * 2 * TotalHoursStorageFor100pcVRE
    ltu      = AllocateLTStorageToVRE * LongTermStorageFor100pcVRE
# in year t, after dispatch
    vre[t] = shr['wnd',t] + shr['sol',t] + shr['ore',t]
    x      = StartingPointWhenLTStorageIsNeeded
    msc[t] = stm * vre[t] * cph[t] + 2 * max(0, vre[t] - x) / (1 - x) ** 2 * cel[t] * ltu
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 3, sub-table J: rows `cbat`, `cint`, `obat`, `elcx`, `eltk`, `elof`, `elov`,
  `cel` (paths, Formulas.md E309-E316), `stm`, `ltu` (A0, E301-E302), `vre`, `cph`, `msc` (E405-E407). Scenario inputs
  `AllocateSTStorageToVRE`, `TotalHoursStorageFor100pcVRE`, `StorageToInterfaceRatioSTStorage`,
  `AllocateLTStorageToVRE`, `StartingPointWhenLTStorageIsNeeded`, `LongTermStorageFor100pcVRE`,
  `StorageHoursForLTStorage`; constant `StMargFactor` (2).
- **CPAT Python:** `power.prepare()` (`stm`, `ltu`, `cel`, `cph`); `power.step()` (`vre`, `msc`); paths in
  `power_data.power_paths()`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: storage"}
- **L4 (fixed).** Legacy applies the 33% allocation of long-term storage twice (rows 3911 and 3912); the model once.
- **Long-term units (LD78).** `LongTermStorageFor100pcVRE` (legacy row 3909) is wired in; before, the factor was 1.
- **M3, M4 (prototype bugs, fixed).** An earlier prototype left out the long-term allocation and the other renewables
  in the VRE share.
- **Scenario settings.** The storage cost per hour and per unit use the ratio, hours and renewables' WACC of the
  scenario (legacy row 3905, J2).
- **Methodology.** The derivative of short-term storage is $18v$ (DOC6) and the long-term table follows the formula
  (DOC7). The methodology states that VRE includes "solar and wind but not hydro (other renewables are neglected)" in
  the short-term subsection, and wind, solar and other renewables elsewhere; the model includes other renewables.
  The methodology's text assumes "a standard 4-hour ratio" for short-term storage in one place and 2 hours in another;
  the model's default is 2.
:::

Data edition Public01:

| | 2022 | 2023 | 2027 | 2030 | 2035 | 2041 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VRE share, scenario 1 | 0.050 | 0.073 | 0.134 | 0.208 | 0.303 | 0.376 |
| VRE share, scenario 2 | 0.050 | 0.074 | 0.135 | 0.188 | 0.284 | 0.361 |
| Cost per marginal hour $c^{ph}$ (USD/kWh) | 0.0062 | 0.0057 | 0.0042 | 0.0035 | | 0.0021 |
| Marginal storage cost $msc$ (USD/kWh), scenario 1 | 0.0056 | 0.0075 | 0.0101 | 0.0129 | 0.0152 | 0.0142 |

Egypt's VRE share stays below 75%, so there is no long-term storage cost. The renewables' discounted lifetime is

In scenario 2 the VRE share is lower than in the baseline from 2030: the carbon price lowers electricity demand and
so the need for new capacity, of which wind and solar are a large part.

## End-user electricity prices {#sec-pw-prices}

Electricity prices start from observed retail prices and then move with the modelled cost of supply. Up to the last
historical price year $L$ the price is the data. After $L$, the price before new policies changes year by year with
the supply cost and with the subsidy components the model tracks, passed through to users at the scenario's
pass-through rate. New policy costs and excises are then added on top, with VAT.

The methodology describes this as concept 4 in
[section 3.4.1.7](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#concept-4-end-user-prices). Its markup
$mu^T = hrp - gnc^{av} - tmc$, with the corrected sign
([corrections, DOC2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/08_Corrections.html#corrections-of-2026-10-31)), is the gap that
the model holds through the subsidy components below, so that the base-year price equals the historical price.

There are two user groups, residential and industry; industry stands for all non-residential users.

### Consumption and supply cost {#sec-pw-supply-cost}

Consumption of each group is its electricity demand in GWh:

$$
cons_{res,t} = \theta_g\, E_{res,t}, \qquad cons_{ind,t} = \theta_g \left(E_t - E_{res,t}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-cons}

(GWh; `cons`). The supply cost adds a transmission and distribution allowance to *last year's* average generation
cost:

$$
sp^T_{g,t} = gnc^{av}_{t-1} + tmc_g, \qquad sp^T_{g,t_0} = gnc^{av}_{t_0} + tmc_g
$$ {#eq-pw-sc}

where $sp^T_{g,t}$ is the supply cost (USD/kWh; `sc`) and $tmc_g$ the transmission and distribution allowance: 0.040
USD/kWh for residential and 0.015 for industrial users (IEA). The one-year lag (link I5) keeps prices free of a
circular reference with dispatch.

### Historical price components {#sec-pw-components}

Up to $L$, the observed price is split into the supply cost and the components that explain the rest. All are held
after $L$, except where stated.

| Component | Definition up to $L$ | After $L$ | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price before VAT $\tilde{p}_{g,t}$ | $hrp_{g,t}/(1 + vatrate_g)$, the retail price of the data × CPI index | held | `rpnv` |
| Price gap $x^{g}_{g,t}$ | $\tilde{p}_{g,t} - sp^T_{g,t} - entx_{g,t}$ | same formula | `txg` |
| Consumer tax or subsidy $x_{g,t}$ | the data's excise and other taxes on electricity × CPI index; without data, $x^{g}_{g,t}$ if `SupplyCostDeltaSubsidy` = Yes, else 0 | held | `txe` |
| Capped supply cost $sp^{cap}_{g,t}$ | $sp^T_{g,t}$ | $\min(sp^T_{g,t},\ sp^{cap}_{g,L})$ | `scl` |
| Producer subsidy per kWh $ps_{g,t}$ | @eq-pw-pseu | $ps_{g,L}\, \phi^{ps}_t$ | `pseu` |
| Consumer subsidy phase-out $cs_{g,t}$ | 0 | @eq-pw-csd | `csd` |
| Residual $ores_{g,t}$ | $x^{g}_{g,t} - x_{g,t} - ps_{g,t}$ | held; a negative one scaled by $sp^{cap}_{g,t}/sp^{cap}_{g,t-1}$ | `ores` |

where $hrp_{g,t}$ is the historical retail price including VAT, $vatrate_g$ the electricity VAT rate of the group (of
the last historical year), $entx_{g,t}$ the manual electricity excise (@eq-pw-entx) and $\phi^{ps}_t$ the phase-out
factor of producer subsidies (`psf`; [M1.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-7)). The residual is the methodology's
"correction for under- or over-estimated transmission and distribution costs".

**Producer subsidy.** The electricity producer subsidy of the data, $PROS_t$ (USD million, positive), is allocated to
the user groups by their pre-tax gap, the amount by which the supply cost exceeds the price before taxes:

$$
a_{g,t} = \frac{\max\left(0,\ sp^T_{g,t} - (\tilde{p}_{g,t} - x_{g,t})\right) cons_{g,t}}
{\sum_{g'} \max\left(0,\ sp^T_{g',t} - (\tilde{p}_{g',t} - x_{g',t})\right) cons_{g',t}}
$$ {#eq-pw-psesh}

$$
ps_{g,t} = \max\left(\underline{ps},\ -\frac{PROS_t\; a_{g,t}}{cons_{g,t}}\right), \qquad t \le L
$$ {#eq-pw-pseu}

where $a_{g,t}$ is the share of group $g$ (`psesh`; if the gaps are all zero, its share of consumption; if that fails,
1 for residential), held after $L$, and $\underline{ps} = -0.3$ USD/kWh the floor (`PsElFloor`). The part beyond the
floor is a memo outside prices, $-PROS_t - \sum_g cons_{g,t}\, ps_{g,t}$ (USD million; `pser`), scaled by
$\phi^{ps}_t$ after $L$. The rows `psegap` and `psegs` hold the numerator and denominator of @eq-pw-psesh.

**Consumer subsidy phase-out.** Where the consumer tax is a subsidy ($x_{g,L} < 0$) and the scenario's
`PowerSubsidyExemptInclude` is Include (the indicator "Include" below), it phases out with the consumer-subsidy
factor $\phi^{cs}_t$ (`pof.cs`):

$$
cs_{g,t} = \mathbb{1}\left[t > L,\ x_{g,t} < 0,\ \text{Include}\right]\; x_{g,t}\left(\phi^{cs}_t - 1\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-csd}

### Price before new policies {#sec-pw-price-before}

Up to $L$ the price is the data; after $L$ it moves with the change in the supply cost and the subsidy components:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{0,T}_{g,t} &= \begin{cases}
hrp_{g,t} & t \le L \\
p^{0,T}_{g,t-1} + \pi \left(X_{g,t} - X_{g,t-1}\right)(1 + vatrate_g) & t > L
\end{cases} \\
X_{g,t} &= sp^T_{g,t} + ps_{g,t} + cs_{g,t} + ores_{g,t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-rppre}

where $p^{0,T}_{g,t}$ is the price before new policies including VAT (USD/kWh real; `rppre`) and $\pi$ =
`PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn` the pass-through of cost changes (default 1). This telescoped form is the legacy price
sum (supply cost + producer subsidy + other tax + residual, then VAT) written as changes; components held at their
last historical values cancel out of the change.

### Excises and the rebate switch {#sec-pw-excise}

Three settings of the scenario add to the price.

**Electricity excise.** In the scenario "Electricity excise" of the scenario table, a per-kWh excise equal to the
carbon price times the grid's base-year CO2 intensity:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x^{e}_t &= \mathbb{1}[\text{policy scenario with electricity excise}]\; \epsilon^{grid}\, \tau_t \\
\epsilon^{grid} &= \frac{\sum_f in_{f,t_0}\, 0.041868\, EF_f}{\sum_f out_{f,t_0}}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-exs}

where $\tau_t$ is the carbon price (USD/tCO2; `cptraj`), $in_{f,t_0}$ the fuel input to power and $out_{f,t_0}$
power output of the base-year energy balance (ktoe, GWh), and $\epsilon^{grid}$ the grid's CO2 intensity (tCO2/kWh;
Egypt 0.00038). Code `exs`.

**Manual excise.** In policy scenarios with `AdditionalExcise` = Yes, the new electricity excise typed on 'Manual
inputs' (real, or nominal × the deflator index if `NomorReal` is not Real), plus the electricity fuel price reform
of the scenario:

$$
entx_{g,t} = \mathbb{1}[o \ne B]\left(\chi^{ae}\; x^{man}_{g,t}\, \delta_t + FPR_{ecy,g,t}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-entx}

where $\chi^{ae}$ is 1 if `AdditionalExcise` = Yes, else 0, $x^{man}_{g,t}$ the typed excise (`entxd`), $\delta_t$ 1
or the deflator index, and $FPR_{ecy,g,t}$ the fuel
price reform path of electricity for the group ([Reforms](#sec-pw-reforms)). Code `entx`. Like legacy, it enters the
price as part of the price before policy: up to $L$ the price data absorb it, and afterwards its change is passed
through. The excise in the price, before VAT, is

$$
pex_{g,t} = x^e_t + \mathbb{1}[t > L]\; \pi\left(entx_{g,t} - entx_{g,L}\right), \qquad pex_{g,t_0} = x^e_{t_0}
$$ {#eq-pw-pex}

(`pex`).

**Rebate switch.** In policy scenarios with `PowerRebates` = Yes (or Yes*), or in a feebate scenario of the scenario
table (Feebates, Power Supply Feebates, Power feebate), the carbon cost is not passed to electricity users:
$rb = 1$ (`rbs`); otherwise $rb = 0$.

### End-user price {#sec-pw-enduser}

The end-user price adds the new policy cost passed through (unless rebated) and the excise, with VAT, and is floored:

$$
p^T_{g,t} = \max\left(p^{0,T}_{g,t} + \left(ncp^{av}_t\, \pi\, (1 - rb) + pex_{g,t}\right)(1 + vatrate_g),\ c_{min}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-rp}

where $p^T_{g,t}$ is the end-user price (USD/kWh real; `rp`), $ncp^{av}_t$ the average new policy cost per kWh
consumed (@eq-pw-gncav) and $c_{min}$ = `MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice` (0.01). VAT is charged on the new policy terms, as
for fuels. The equation list has the price as ([M4.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M4-7)) and with the subsidy components
and floor as ([A4.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-8)).

### Subsidy gap and the supply cost of the subsidy lines {#sec-pw-sgap}

The subsidy gap compares the price before VAT with the modelled supply cost; a negative gap means the price is below
cost, a subsidy:

$$
gap_{g,t} = \frac{p^{0,T}_{g,t}}{1 + vatrate_g} - sp^T_{g,t}
$$ {#eq-pw-sgap}

(USD/kWh; `sgap`). The supply cost read by the subsidy and efficient-price lines of the welfare block (@sec-fiscal)
removes the residual and adds the policy terms:

$$
sp^{e}_{g,t} = sp^T_{g,t} + ores_{g,t} + ncp^{av}_t\, \pi\, (1 - rb) + pex_{g,t}
$$ {#eq-pw-spe}

(`spe`).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: end-user prices"}
```
for t in years:
    cons['res',t] = dem['res',t] * 11.63;  cons['ind',t] = (demtot[t] - dem['res',t]) * 11.63
    for g in ['res', 'ind']:
        sc[g,t]   = (gncav[t] if t == base_year else gncav[t-1]) + tmc[g]
        pex[g,t]  = exs[t] + (pass_on * (entx[g,t] - entx[g,L]) if t > L else 0)
        rpnv[g,t] = rp_data[g,t] / (1 + vat[g]) if t <= L else rpnv[g,t-1]
        txg[g,t]  = rpnv[g,t] - sc[g,t] - entx[g,t]
        txe[g,t]  = (tx_data[g,t] if has data else txg[g,t] * (SupplyCostDeltaSubsidy == 'Yes')) if t <= L else txe[g,t-1]
        scl[g,t]  = sc[g,t] if t <= L else min(sc[g,t], scl[g,L])
        psegap[g,t] = max(0, sc[g,t] - (rpnv[g,t] - txe[g,t])) * cons[g,t]
    for g in ['res', 'ind']:
        if t <= L:
            psesh[g,t] = psegap[g,t] / sum(psegap) or cons[g,t] / sum(cons) or (1 if g == 'res' else 0)
            pseu[g,t]  = max(PsElFloor, -pros_ecy[t] * psesh[g,t] / cons[g,t])
        else:
            psesh[g,t] = psesh[g,t-1];  pseu[g,t] = pseu[g,L] * psf[t]
    pser[t] = -pros_ecy[t] - sum(cons[g,t] * pseu[g,t]) if t <= L else pser[L] * psf[t]
    for g in ['res', 'ind']:
        csd[g,t]  = txe[g,t] * (pof_cs[t] - 1) if t > L and txe[g,t] < 0 and PowerSubsidyExemptInclude == 'Include' else 0
        if t <= L:  ores[g,t] = txg[g,t] - txe[g,t] - pseu[g,t]
        else:       ores[g,t] = ores[g,t-1] * scl[g,t] / scl[g,t-1] if ores[g,t-1] < 0 else ores[g,t-1]
        X = lambda k: sc[g,k] + pseu[g,k] + csd[g,k] + ores[g,k]
        rppre[g,t] = rp_data[g,t] if t <= L else rppre[g,t-1] + pass_on * (X(t) - X(t-1)) * (1 + vat[g])
        rp[g,t]    = max(rppre[g,t] + (ccpav[t] * pass_on * (1 - rbs) + pex[g,t]) * (1 + vat[g]), MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice)
        sgap[g,t]  = rppre[g,t] / (1 + vat[g]) - sc[g,t]
        spe[g,t]   = sc[g,t] + ores[g,t] + ccpav[t] * pass_on * (1 - rbs) + pex[g,t]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 3, sub-table G: rows `cons`, `sc`, `rppre`, `entxd`, `entx`, `pex`, `rp`,
  `sgap`, `rpnv`, `txg`, `txe`, `scl`, `psegap`, `psegs`, `psesh`, `pseu`, `pser`, `csd`, `ores`, `spe` (Formulas.md
  E356-E363, E372-E383; LAMBDAs `HISTHOLD`, `PRICEGAP`, `ELTAXBASE`, `CAPLAST`, `PREGAP`, `PSALLOC`, `PSELEC`,
  `PSERESID`, `CSELEC`, `ORESID`, `ELSUPPLY`); `rbs`, `exs` in A0. User groups on Inputs rows 220-222 (weights,
  transmission cost, VAT rate, historical prices 2021-2024), grid intensity `PwGInt`, constant `PsElFloor`. Scenario
  inputs `PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn`, `MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice`, `PowerRebates`, `AdditionalExcise`,

  `entx` in `power.prepare()` (EQ-A4.7); user groups in `power_data.user_groups()`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: end-user prices"}
- **S4, LD32 (same numbers).** Legacy computes the residential and industrial price as supply cost + producer subsidy
  + other tax + "over/under-estimated costs" residual, then VAT (rows 3600-3617 and 3629-3646). The model telescopes
  it: after the last historical year the price changes by pass-through × the change in (supply cost + producer
  subsidy + consumer-subsidy phase-out + residual) × (1 + VAT); the held components cancel. The residual is held, a
  negative one scaled by the capped supply cost, as legacy 465 rows 3607 and 3636 (O3607: `MIN(0, O3600 - $J3600)`).
- **Pass-through.** Legacy hardcodes the pass-through of the price chain to 1 in places; the model uses
  `PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn` of the scenario (default 1) throughout. The price-control factor of the fuel blocks
  does not act on electricity prices; the methodology's text says price-control settings diminish all price changes.
- **Producer subsidies (LD19, R7).** As legacy: allocation by the pre-tax gap (rows 3587-3589), per kWh floored at
  −0.3 USD/kWh (rows 3590-3591; issue I146), residual memo (row 3592), passed through in the price before policies
  (rows 3601, 3630). Legacy bugs not reproduced: **L83** (the producer subsidy compounds the factor and lags a year),
  **L86** (no manual override for the electricity producer subsidy).
- **Consumer subsidy (R9).** As legacy O3606, O3635; legacy bugs not reproduced: **L84** (consumer subsidy phased with
  the price-control factor; option text mismatch), **L85** (info row subtracts industry).
- **Subsidy gap (S7).** Legacy holds producer-side subsidies and the residual as rows; the model also reports one
  subsidy gap, price before VAT − supply cost, for revenue analysis.
- **VAT on the policy terms (decision 2).** Legacy charges VAT on the new policy terms (row 3614); the model does too,
  as for fuels.
- **Rebate (LD77).** Legacy rows 261, 2188, J3595. Switches accept Yes or Yes* (bug L113 / issue I58: legacy tests the
  exact "Yes").
- **Excises (LD77, I59).** The electricity excise as legacy rows 2190, 2253; the manual excise as legacy rows 195-217,
  3602, 3631. The fuel price reform of electricity enters the manual excise (issue I59, replicated).
- **Floor (I60).** End-user prices are floored at `MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice` as legacy rows 3617 and 3646 (issue I60,
  replicated; not binding for Egypt).
- **Historical prices (decision 3, LD33).** The model uses the corrected price data block. For Egypt the earlier
  prototype data had residential prices of 0.054, 0.048, 0.043 USD/kWh nominal (2022-2024) where legacy 456's vintage
  had 0.097 in 2022; with the legacy 465 data the prices are the same as legacy (LD33).
- **Producer subsidy data (decision 4).** The earlier corrected block had no electricity producer subsidy where legacy
  456 used −9.2 bn USD in 2022; the model reports the modelled subsidy gap in any case (S7).
- **Methodology.** Markup sign corrected (DOC2). The methodology's end-user price adds the generation cost of the year;
  the model, as legacy, the cost of the previous year.
:::

## Power revenues {#sec-pw-revenues}

The power sector adds to government revenue in two ways: through the electricity bills of users (VAT, excises, the
carbon cost passed through, rebates, the subsidy gap) and through the fuels and emissions of generation (taxes and
subsidies on generation fuels, existing carbon pricing, new policies, renewable subsidies). Both are computed here, in
USD million real, and added to the revenue totals in @sec-fiscal.

### By user group {#sec-pw-revenues-users}

Each term is a per-kWh amount times consumption $cons_{g,t}$ (GWh; GWh × USD/kWh = USD million):

| Revenue | Per kWh | Code |
|---|---|---|
| VAT on the price before new policies | $p^{0,T}_{g,t}\, vatrate_g/(1 + vatrate_g)$ | `rvat` |
| VAT on the new-policy cost and excise passed through | $\left(ncp^{av}_t\, \pi\, (1 - rb) + pex_{g,t}\right) vatrate_g$ | `rnvat` |
| Rebate (negative): the carbon cost returned to users | $-rb\; ncp^{av}_t\, \pi$ | `rreb` |
| Excise | $pex_{g,t}$; of which carbon-based excise $x^e_t$ (`rexs`, all users) and manual excise (`rexm` = total − `rexs`) | `rpex` |
| Subsidy gap (signed: negative = fiscal cost) | $gap_{g,t}$ | `rgap` |
| New-policy cost (memo, ETS at the tax-equivalent price) | $ncp^{av}_t$ | `rcarb` |

The VAT on a rebated carbon cost is not collected.

### By generation type {#sec-pw-revenues-types}

With a fuel flag $\chi_f$ = 1 for coal, gas, oil and biomass and 0 otherwise:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^{tax}_{f,t} &= \chi_f\, FU_{f,t}\, \kappa_{PJ}\, (etx + vat)_{c(f),t} \\
R^{sub}_{f,t} &= \chi_f\, FU_{f,t}\, \kappa_{PJ}\, esub_{c(f),t} \\
R^{xc}_{f,t} &= 8.76\; gen_{f,t}\; \Delta xcp_{f,t} \\
R^{new}_{f,t} &= 8.76\; gen_{f,t}\; ncp_{f,t} - CO2_{f,t}\, A_{pow,t}\, (1 - \rho^{ets}_t) \\
R^{xl}_{f,t} &= CO2_{f,t} \left(XCT_{f,t}\,\phi^{ct}_t + XETS_{f,t}\,\phi^{ets}_t\right) \\
R^{rns}_{f,t} &= 8.76\; gen_{f,t}\; rns_{f,t}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-revenues}

where

- $R^{tax}$ are existing taxes on generation fuels (excise and other taxes plus VAT of the price fuel $c(f)$, USD/GJ;
  `prtx`) and $R^{sub}$ existing subsidies (negative; `prsub`), with $\kappa_{PJ}$ = 0.041868 PJ per ktoe;
- $R^{xc}$ the change in existing carbon pricing against the price data (`prxc`);
- $R^{new}$ new-policy revenue (`prnew`): carbon tax, ETS and fuel price reform per kWh times generation, less the
  part of the ETS cost not collected, so that the ETS is valued at the permit price as in the subsectors; $\rho^{ets}_t$
  is the ETS revenue factor (`ets.rf`, @sec-emissions);
- $R^{xl}$ the level of existing carbon pricing (memo; `prxl`);
- $R^{rns}$ renewable subsidies (negative; `prrns`).

Fuel use of generation, $\sum_f \chi_f FU_{f,t}$, is the power row of the fuel totals (`pet`). The equation list has
the revenues by type as ([A6.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A6-1)).

### Into the revenue totals {#sec-pw-revenues-totals}

The revenue totals (@sec-fiscal) add a power row:

| Total | Power part |
|---|---|
| Existing taxes | fuel taxes $R^{tax}$ + change in existing carbon pricing $R^{xc}$ + electricity VAT `rvat` |
| Subsidies | fuel subsidies $R^{sub}$ + subsidy gap `rgap` + renewable subsidies $R^{rns}$ |
| New policies | new-policy revenue $R^{new}$ + VAT on new policies `rnvat` + rebate `rreb` + excise `rpex` |
| Existing carbon pricing level | the memo $R^{xl}$ |

In the revenue by policy, the rebate and the carbon-based excise count with the carbon tax, the manual excise with the
excise, and the renewable subsidies in their own row (the base subsidy once). The fuel subsidy and the subsidy gap do
not overlap: the supply cost already uses the subsidised fuel price, so the gap is what remains between that cost and
the tariff.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: power revenues"}
```
for t in years:
    for g in ['res', 'ind']:
        passed     = ccpav[t] * pass_on * (1 - rbs)
        rvat[g,t]  = rppre[g,t] * vat[g] / (1 + vat[g]) * cons[g,t]
        rnvat[g,t] = (passed + pex[g,t]) * vat[g] * cons[g,t]
        rreb[g,t]  = -rbs * ccpav[t] * pass_on * cons[g,t]
        rpex[g,t]  = pex[g,t] * cons[g,t]
        rgap[g,t]  = sgap[g,t] * cons[g,t]
        rcarb[g,t] = ccpav[t] * cons[g,t]
    rexs[t] = exs[t] * sum(cons[g,t]);  rexm[t] = sum(rpex[g,t]) - rexs[t]
    for f in types:
        c = price_fuel[f]
        prtx[f,t]  = fflag[f] * pe[f,t] * 0.041868 * (etx[c,t] + vat_fuel[c,t])
        prsub[f,t] = fflag[f] * pe[f,t] * 0.041868 * esub[c,t]
        prxc[f,t]  = xck[f,t] * 8.76 * gen[f,t]
        prnew[f,t] = gen[f,t] * 8.76 * xac[f,t] - co2[f,t] * etr['pow',t] * (1 - ets_rf[t])
        prxl[f,t]  = co2[f,t] * (xct[f,t] * xct_p[t] + xets[f,t] * xets_p[t])
        prrns[f,t] = rns[f,t] * 8.76 * gen[f,t]
    pet[t] = sum(pe[f,t] * fflag[f] for f in types)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 3, sub-tables G4 (rows `rcarb`, `rexs`, `rexm`, `rvat`, `rnvat`, `rreb`,
  `rpex`, `rgap`; Formulas.md E364-E371) and M (rows `prtx`, `prsub`, `prxc`, `prnew`, `prxl`, `prrns`, `pet`;
  E439-E445). The revenue totals in section 12 and the revenue by policy in block 12e.
- **CPAT Python:** `power.step()`, blocks "end-user prices" (user groups) and "revenues of the power sector"
  (EQ-A6.1); totals in `totals.revenues`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: power revenues"}
- **M6, LD35 (fixed).** An earlier prototype valued the power ETS revenue at the tax-equivalent price; the model values
  it at the permit price, as the subsectors (`rcarb`, at the tax-equivalent price, is kept as a memo).
- **M2 (fixed).** An earlier prototype left out the VAT on the policy term.
- **L110 (fixed).** Legacy's power revenue rebate counts VAT that was never collected (row 3663); in the model the
  rebate is the carbon cost × pass-through, and its VAT falls out of `rnvat`.
- **L111 (fixed).** Legacy's manual electricity excise revenue counts the whole excise, also where the price does not
  include it (rows 3660, 7762); the model counts the excise in the price × consumption.
- **L108, L129 (fixed).** Legacy's cost of renewable subsidies counts the base subsidy twice, ignores the hydro switch
  and omits biomass (rows 3665-3669, 7897-7903); the model counts subsidy × generation by type, the base subsidy once.
- **Revenue by policy.** The rebate and the carbon-based excise count with the carbon tax, the manual excise with the
  excise, the renewable subsidies in their own row, as legacy rows 7749, 7762, 7903.
- **New rows.** Taxes and subsidies on generation fuels, the change in existing carbon pricing, VAT, VAT on new
  policies and the subsidy gap are new (legacy has no such power revenue rows). Revenue structure as legacy (LD37),
  power in the totals (LD39).
:::

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Subsidy gap, residential, scenario 1 | −4,127 | −6,686 | −6,927 | −7,642 | −11,225 |

## The coal implicit cost {#sec-pw-coalic}

A model with one period per year cannot see why many countries burn less coal than its cost advantage suggests:
environmental regulation of coal plants, and the flexibility gas offers. CPAT therefore adds an implicit cost to coal,
calibrated so that the model reproduces observed coal shares.

The methodology describes the calibration in
[section 3.4.2.4.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#calibration-and-systems-costs) and writes the
cost $ipc$ ([corrections, DOC12](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/08_Corrections.html#corrections-of-2026-10-31)).

The cost moves linearly from a short-term value in the base year to a long-term value in 2030:

$$
ipc_t = ipc^{S} + \left(ipc^{L} - ipc^{S}\right) \min\left(1,\ \frac{t - t_0}{T_{ic} - t_0}\right)
$$ {#eq-pw-cic}

where

- $ipc_t$ is the coal implicit cost (USD/kWh; `cic`);
- $ipc^{S}$ and $ipc^{L}$ are the short-term and long-term values (`cics`, `cicl`), chosen by the scenario input
  `AdditionalCoalIntangibleCost`: No gives 0; Manual gives `ManualCoalIntangibleCostST` and
  `ManualCoalIntangibleCostLT`; otherwise the country's values in the GoalSeekCoal table (85 countries; 0 if the
  country is absent, as for Egypt);
- $T_{ic}$ = 2030 (`CoalICYr`).

The cost is added to the coal variable cost (@eq-pw-vbc), so it acts on dispatch, on the levelised variable cost and
so on investment, and on early coal retirement. It is also part of the generation cost and so of tariffs, unless the
setting `PwCoalICTariff` is No (default Yes, as legacy; @eq-pw-gnc). It appears in the system cost memo.

The methodology's calibration minimises the squared difference between modelled and observed (IEA) coal shares in
2019 and 2020, raising the coal price where the model overestimates the coal share (only positive values); the
GoalSeekCoal table reports the results for both years, and IEA's 2030 projection of the coal share is reported for
information. The model uses legacy's stored results; the calibration itself (a goal seek) is not part of the model.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 3, sub-table D: rows `cics`, `cicl`, `cic` (Formulas.md E325-E327; names
  `CoalICSTc`, `CoalICLTc` on the GoalSeekCoal tab, columns B and C); Settings C66 `PwCoalICTariff`; constant
  `CoalICYr`.
- **CPAT Python:** `power.prepare()` (table `coal_implicit_price`, columns `first_year`, `year_2030`); the tariff
  switch is the module constant `COAL_IC_TARIFF` (Yes).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: coal implicit cost"}
- **As legacy (LD34).** Rows 3360-3363 (D3), with J89:K90 choosing the short- and long-term values and K88 the year
  2030. Legacy ScenarioDefinition rows 369-371 hold the option and the manual values.
- **Not built.** The calibration script (goal seek) that fills GoalSeekCoal: the stored legacy values are used.
:::

## Fuel price reform, price floor and renewable subsidies in real terms {#sec-pw-reforms}

Four smaller rules complete the price side. Each is described where it acts; this section collects them.

| Rule | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Electricity fuel price reform | The fuel price reform path of electricity of the scenario, by user group (`fpr.ecy.res`, `fpr.ecy.ind`), enters the manual excise of policy scenarios (issue I59, replicated) | @eq-pw-entx |
| Price floor | End-user electricity prices are floored at `MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice` (0.01 USD/kWh; issue I60, replicated; not binding for Egypt) | @eq-pw-rp |
| Renewable subsidies in real terms | The renewable subsidy inputs, labelled nominal, are converted to real with the CPI factor of the year (row `rnsp`; legacy bug L114 fixed) | @eq-pw-rns |
| Transmission cost share | The levelised cost includes `TransmissionCostShare` (default 1) of the transmission capex | @eq-pw-lfx |

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT: reforms and subsidies"}
- **Fuel price reform (I59).** As legacy row 216; inputs in the fuel price reform block of the scenario sheet (legacy
  ScenarioDefinition rows 148-149, 162-163).
- **Floor (I60).** As legacy rows 3617 and 3646.
- **Renewable subsidies (L114, L107, LD76).** Legacy uses the nominal inputs (ScenarioDefinition 354-355) as real
  (L114, was issue I55): fixed. Legacy's additional subsidy starts in the consumer-subsidy phase-out year (L107):
  the model uses its own start year `RenSubsidyAddStartYear` (default 2027, the default of the consumer-subsidy year).
- **Transmission share.** Legacy `IncludeTransmissionCostsInGenerationCostsPercent`; the model reads
  `TransmissionCostShare` from the scenario sheet's appendix block B.
:::

## Power data: how the inputs are derived {#sec-pw-data}

Before the year loop, a data step derives the power inputs of the country from the reference tables: the technology
data of the legacy Power tab, the cost-of-capital (CoC) tab, the energy balance, installed capacity, the GHGs tab
(demand shock), WEO (income factor) and the scenario settings. Excel-AI computes them with formulas on its Inputs
sheet; CPAT Python computes the same in `power_data.py`. Nothing is copied from a legacy run.

The methodology describes the data in
[section 3.4.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-PowerDataSources): the sources, the data
approach of the engineer model
([3.4.4.1.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#data-approach-for-the-power-prices-and-engineer-power-model)),
the variables ([3.4.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#description-and-definition-of-the-variables))
and the estimation of the power-sector characteristics
([3.4.4.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-PowerCharacteristics)).

The inputs fall into three groups, named after the tables they once were:

| Group | Contents | Excel-AI block | Python function |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generation-type items (PowerTech) | One row per type: costs, lifetime, efficiency, capacity factor, WACC, base-year capacity and generation, retirement, investment and scale-up rules | `Inputs_ptech` | `power_tech()` |
| Year paths (PowerPaths) | Capex time factors, storage costs, income factor, demand shock, planned retirement | `Inputs_ppath` | `power_paths()` |
| Parameters (PowerParams) | Transmission costs, pass-through, storage settings, shares of the energy balance, logit constants and other settings | `Inputs_ppar` | `power_params()` |

The settings of scenario 1 and values derived from them are a fourth, small block (`Inputs_pset`, names `Ps...`;
`power_settings()`). The derived constants that section 3 reads (Inputs rows 207-215, 220-234, 254-263) follow
(`power_types()`, `user_groups()`, `demand_groups()`, `demand_subsectors()`, `system_params()`). The equation list
has the data steps as ([A4.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-1)) to ([A4.4](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-4)).

Five rules of the data step depart from legacy CPAT, which has bugs in these chains (register L52-L56): the country
value is used for every type where it exists (L52), the actual capacity factor is used within its bounds (L53), hydro
invests from the base year only above a 50% hydro share (L54), country rows are looked up in the country block (L55),
and countries without cost-of-capital risk data take the default WACC (L56). The legacy chains, cell by cell, are in
the collapsed boxes at the end of this section.

### Technoeconomic parameters {#sec-pw-data-tech}

The study data of the Power tab give, for each type, a world value and, for some countries, a country value. The
country value is used where it is positive; otherwise the world value ("rule C"):

$$
x_f = \begin{cases} x^{country}_f & \text{if } x^{country}_f > 0 \\ x^{world}_f & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-pw-rulec}

for $x$ in: capacity factor of the studies, capital cost (USD/kW), efficiency (net calorific value) of the studies,
fixed O&M (USD/kW/year), variable O&M (USD/kWh), WACC of the studies and lifetime (years). The country rows have codes
`<iso>.mpp.<type>` (63 countries), the world rows `wld.mpp.<type>`; the regional rows are not used. Wind, solar, hydro
and other renewables have a studies efficiency of 1 by convention.

Decommissioning cost and transmission capex are world shares of the capital cost:
$dtc_f = \delta^{dtc}_f\, cax^0_f$ and $tcx_f = \delta^{tcx}_f\, cax^0_f$, with $\delta$ from the world rows
`wld.dtc.<type>` (the shares of biomass and other renewables are averages of the others). Fixed O&M per kWh is
$opf_f = opf^{kW}_f/(H\, cf_f)$. Nuclear has a fixed fuel cost of 0.004 USD/kWh (`UraniumFuel`).

Values for Egypt (data edition Public01):

| | Coal | Gas | Oil | Nuclear | Wind | Solar | Hydro | Other ren. | Biomass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capital cost $cax^0$ (USD/kW) | 2,000 | 1,304.2 | 1,345.4 | 4,000 | 1,300 | 1,222.7 | 3,300 | 3,500 | 2,000 |
| Lifetime (years) | 30 | 30 | 35 | 50 | 30 | 25 | 50 | 30 | 30 |
| Fixed O&M (USD/kW/year) | 60 | 32.05 | 23.525 | 150 | 40 | 11.831 | 50 | 100 | 100 |
| Variable O&M (USD/kWh) | 0.003 | 0.004 | 0.00517 | 0.004 | 0 | 0 | 0.001 | 0 | 0.003 |
| Studies capacity factor | 0.535 | 0.566 | 0.134 | 0.934 | 0.3 | 0.18 | 0.432 | 0.751 | 0.686 |
| Studies efficiency | 0.344 | 0.594 | 0.377 | 0.38 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.253 |
| Decommissioning $dtc$ (USD/kW) | 100 | 13.04 | 33.02 | 532.13 | 39 | 73.36 | 660 | 253.79 | 145.02 |
| Transmission $tcx$ (USD/kW) | 597.47 | 382.18 | 447.88 | 449.43 | 405.47 | 335.33 | 756.53 | 347.66 | 267.62 |

Gas (row `egy.mpp.nga`) and solar (`egy.mpp.sol`) have country values; the country gas row has no capacity factor,
WACC or lifetime, so those fall back to the world.

### Energy balance: generation, efficiency, capacity factor and capacity {#sec-pw-data-balance}

Base-year generation, fuel input and installed capacity give the actual efficiency and capacity factor
([methodology, 3.4.4.1.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#data-approach-for-the-power-prices-and-engineer-power-model)):

$$
\begin{aligned}
gen_{f,t_0} &= out_f\, \frac{1000}{H}, \qquad & \nu^{a}_f &= \frac{out_f}{in_f\, \theta_g} \\
cf^{a}_f &= \frac{gen_{f,t_0}}{IC_f}, \qquad & cap_{f,t_0} &= \frac{gen_{f,t_0}}{cf_f}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-balance}

where

- $out_f$ is power output of the energy balance (GWh, flow `eloutput`) and $in_f$ fuel input to power (ktoe, minus the
  flow `power`), for the type's fuels (oil: other oil products, gasoline, diesel, kerosene, LPG, jet fuel);
- $gen_{f,t_0}$ base-year generation (MWy);
- $\nu^a_f$ the actual efficiency, used unless below the minimum or without input (@sec-pw-a0);
- $IC_f$ installed capacity of the base year (MW, Power tab installed-capacity block);
- $cf^a_f$ the actual capacity factor, used within its bounds (@eq-pw-cf);
- $cap_{f,t_0}$ base-year capacity at the capacity factor used.

Values for Egypt (data edition Public01, base year 2022):

| | Gas | Oil | Wind | Solar | Hydro |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base-year generation (MWy) | 19,165 | 2,089 | 666 | 555 | 1,717 |
| Installed capacity $IC$ (MW) | 52,020 | 1,330 | 1,643 | 1,724 | 2,832 |
| Actual capacity factor | 0.368 | 1.571 | 0.406 | 0.322 | 0.606 |
| Capacity factor used | 0.368 | 0.134 (studies) | 0.406 | 0.322 | 0.606 |
| Efficiency used | 0.505 | 0.338 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Base-year capacity (MW) | 52,020 | 15,590 | 1,643 | 1,724 | 2,832 |

Coal (10 MW installed), nuclear, other renewables and biomass (123 MW installed) generate nothing in the base year.
Oil's actual capacity factor is above 1, outside the bounds, so the studies value is used and the base-year oil
capacity is the generation-consistent 15,590 MW, not the installed 1,330 MW.

### Capex time factors {#sec-pw-data-ctf}

The capital cost path of each type is its world capex time factor, by year (for wind and solar 1.05 in 2022 and 1 in
2023). Renewables (wind, solar, hydro, other renewables, biomass) take the series of the
decline scenario `RenewableCostDeclineRate` (low, medium*, high, very high); coal, gas, oil and nuclear take the
medium series. Where the Power tab has no series for the option (low and very high for wind and solar, very high
for the others), wind and solar take the older series of the same option (`wld.ctf.old<scen>.<type>`) and the others
the medium series (LD79). The country never matters: there are no country series.

For Egypt (medium), wind falls from 1.05 (2022) to 0.918 (2041) and solar from 1.05 to 0.565; the other types stay at 1.

### WACC {#sec-pw-data-wacc}

The country WACC is the real WACC of the CoC tab for 2022 (constant over time). It is computed by the WACC
calculator: the cost of equity $r_f + \beta (ERP_{US} + CRP)$ weighted by the equity share, plus the cost of debt
$(r_f + \text{default spread} + \text{lender margin})(1 - \text{tax})(1 - \text{equity share})$, with $r_f$ the real
risk-free rate. A country missing from CoC, or without CoC risk data (rating "Not Found"), takes the default 0.075
(`WaccDefault`; L56).

The technology premium depends on the type and the World Bank income group of the country:

| Type | bio | nga | coa | ore | hyd | sol | oil | nuc | wnd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Premium, LMIC | 0.03215 | 0.02465 | 0.02465 | 0.04425 | 0.02725 | 0.02935 | 0.02465 | 0.02725 | 0.02935 |

(columns HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC in the CoC table). The income-group WACC of the option Income* is HIC 0.075, UMIC 0.10,
LMIC 0.125, LIC 0.15.

For Egypt (LMIC, $w_c$ = 0.0994764, option Tech): coal, gas and oil 0.12413; nuclear and hydro 0.12673; wind and solar
0.12883; other renewables 0.14373; biomass 0.13163.

### Generation-type items {#sec-pw-data-types}

| Item | Meaning | Rule | Country-specific? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cax0` | Capital cost at time factor 1 (USD/kW) | rule C on the capital cost | yes, via a country row |
| `life` | Lifetime (years) | rule C | where the country row has it |
| `eff` | Efficiency | actual from the balance, else studies (rule C; 1 for wind, solar, hydro, other renewables) | yes (balance) |
| `cf` | Capacity factor | actual within the bounds, else studies (rule C) | yes (balance, installed capacity) |
| `wacc` | WACC | by `WACCSource` (@eq-pw-wacc) | yes (CoC) |
| `dtc`, `tcx` | Decommissioning, transmission capex (USD/kW) | world share × capital cost | via the capital cost |
| `opf` | Fixed O&M per kWh | fixed O&M / (8,760 × capacity factor) | via O&M and capacity factor |
| `vop` | Variable O&M (USD/kWh) | rule C | where the country row has it |
| `ffix` | Fixed fuel cost (USD/kWh) | nuclear 0.004, others 0 | no |
| `cap0`, `gen0` | Base-year capacity (MW), generation (MWy) | @eq-pw-balance | yes |
| `rr` | Retirement rate | $1/N$; hydro 0 if `HydroDoesntRetire` = Yes | via lifetime |
| `permitted`, `start` | Investment permitted, first year | [Inputs of the scenario](#sec-pw-a0) | yes (capacity and generation shares) |
| `scaleup` | Scale-up rate | [Inputs of the scenario](#sec-pw-a0) | wind and solar under CtryDefault* |
| `planned` | Planned retirement used | coal: the country flag of the Power tab; others No | yes (coal) |
| `rns` | Renewable subsidy | 0 (the subsidy is a scenario input) | no |
| `price_code`, `vre`, `vre_share`, `dispatch` | Price fuel (`coa.pow`, `nga.pow`, `oop.all`, `bio.all`), VRE flags (wind, solar, other renewables), dispatch group (coal, gas) | constants of the type table | no |

### Year paths {#sec-pw-data-paths}

| Path | Meaning | Source and rule |
|---|---|---|
| `tcf\|<type>` | Capex time factor | [Capex time factors](#sec-pw-data-ctf) |
| `cbat`, `cint`, `obat` | Battery capex (USD/kWh), battery interface capex (USD/kW), battery fixed opex (USD/kWh/year) | Power tab battery block, the latest year not after the model year; EUR converted to USD at 1.18 (2021) |
| `elcx`, `eltk`, `elof`, `elov` | Electrolyser capex (USD/kW), storage tank capex (USD/kWh), electrolyser fixed and variable opex | as above |
| `cel` | Long-term storage cost per marginal unit | @eq-pw-cel, with `StorageHoursForLTStorage` and the renewables' discounted lifetime (country WACC) |
| `incf` | Income factor on the GDP elasticities | @eq-pw-incf |
| `shock` | Exogenous shock on energy demand | GHGs tab: 2023 and 2024 values of the country; 0 in other years |
| `pret\|<type>` | Planned retirement (nameplate MW) | coal: the Power tab averaged block where the country flag is Yes; otherwise 0 |

**Income factor.** The GDP elasticity of demand falls with income. The factor is a quartic polynomial in log GDP per
capita, normalised:

$$
\begin{aligned}
inc_t &= \frac{\max\left(0,\ P_4(x_t)\right)}{0.74}, \qquad x_t = \min\left(10,\ \ln y^{pc}_{t-1}\right) \\
P_4(x) &= 0.012019x^4 - 0.365464x^3 + 4.011846x^2 \\
&\quad - 18.722243x + 31.75949
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-incf}

where $y^{pc}_{t-1}$ is GDP per capita of the previous year (USD; the base year uses its own year), from the macro
series. The factor applies if `IncElAdj` is Yes (default Yes*), else 1. It is used by power demand and by fuel use.
For Egypt it falls from 1.027 (2022) to 0.946 (2041).

**Demand shock.** For Egypt, −0.2081 in 2023 and +0.0924 in 2024.

### Parameters {#sec-pw-data-params}

| Parameter | Meaning | Source | Egypt |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tmc\|res`, `tmc\|ind` | Transmission and distribution allowance (USD/kWh) | Power tab G20, G21 | 0.04, 0.015 |
| `pass` | Pass-through of cost changes | `PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn` | 1 |
| `gen_per_cons` | Generation / final demand of the base year | energy balance | 1.266 |
| `dlf_ren` | Discounted lifetime of renewables | average of wind and solar | 8.435 |
| `st_alloc`, `st_marg_hours`, `st_ratio` | Short-term storage allocation, marginal hours (2 × hours for 100% VRE), kWh per kW | settings | 1, 18, 2 |
| `lt_start`, `lt_alloc` | Long-term storage threshold, allocation | settings | 0.75, 0.33 |
| `sh_nxp`, `sh_tsd`, `sh_eou`, `sh_add` | Shares of final demand (@eq-pw-shares) | energy balance | 0.0094, 0.2168, 0.0400, 0 |
| `extra_eff` | Additional efficiency gain | `AdditionalEfficiencyPower` | 0 |
| `maxcf_cg` | Maximum capacity factor of coal (gas has its own input) | `MaximumCoalCF` | 0.9 |
| `k_dispatch`, `k_invest` | Logit constants | `kDispatch`, `kInvestment` | 2, 2 |
| `min_cost` | Minimum cost and price | `MinPostSubsidyPowerPrice` | 0.01 |
| `early_max` | Maximum early coal retirement share | constant `EarlyMaxShare` | 0.8 |
| `early_factor` | Early-retirement factor of the baseline | `MaxCostBasedEarlyRetirement` if `EarlyRetirementInBaseline` = Yes, else 0 | 0.8 |
| `ktoe_gwh` | GWh per ktoe | constant | 11.63 |

The shares of final demand come from the base-year energy balance of electricity:

$$
\begin{aligned}
s_{nxp} &= -\frac{M + X}{D}, \qquad s_{tsd} = -\frac{SD + TR + DL}{D}, \qquad s_{eou} = -\frac{OU}{D} \\
s_{add} &= \frac{G}{D} - 1 - s_{nxp} - s_{tsd} - s_{eou}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pw-shares}

where $M$, $X$, $SD$, $TR$, $DL$, $OU$ are imports, exports, statistical differences, transfers, distribution losses
and own use of electricity (ktoe, with the energy balance's signs), $G = \sum_f gen_{f,t_0} \cdot 8.76/11.63$ base-year
generation (ktoe) and $D$ final electricity demand (ktoe): the sum over the flows road, rail, domestic aviation,
domestic navigation, residential, food and forestry, services, mining and chemicals, iron and steel, non-ferrous
metals, machinery, cement, other manufacturing, construction and other non-specified (fuel transformation, own use and
non-energy use excluded). So $1 + s_{nxp} + s_{tsd} + s_{eou} + s_{add} = G/D$ exactly. The equation list has them
as ([A4.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-3)).

The grid CO2 intensity of the electricity excise (@eq-pw-exs) and the required-generation factor (@eq-pw-req) are
derived from these parameters.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: the power data of a country"}
```
bal = energy_balance(country, base_year)
for f in types:
    w, c = world_row[f], country_row[f] or w
    pick = lambda col: c[col] if c[col] > 0 else w[col]                 # rule C
    cax0[f], life[f], opfx[f], vop[f] = pick('CapEx'), pick('Lifetime'), pick('OpexFixed'), pick('OpexVariable')
    cf_studies[f], wacc_studies[f]   = pick('CapacityFactor'), pick('WACC')
    eff_studies[f] = 1 if f in ('wnd','sol','hyd','ore') else pick('Efficiency')
    out[f] = sum(bal['eloutput'][x] for x in fuels[f]);  inp[f] = -sum(bal['power'][x] for x in fuels[f])
    eff_act  = out[f] / (inp[f] * 11.63) if inp[f] else None
    eff[f]   = eff_studies[f] if eff_act is None or eff_act < MinimumThermalEfficiency else eff_act
    gen0[f]  = out[f] * 1000 / 8760
    cf_act   = gen0[f] / installed_capacity[f] if installed_capacity[f] else 0
    cf[f]    = cf_act if cf_min[f] < cf_act < CFOverrideIfAbove else cf_studies[f]
    wacc[f]  = (w_cty + adj['coa', inc] if WACCSource == 'Country*' else
                w_cty + adj[f, inc] if WACCSource == 'Tech' else
                max(WACCUserGlobal if WACCSource == 'User' else w_income[inc] if WACCSource == 'Income*'
                    else wacc_studies[f], MinimumWACC))
    dtc[f], tcx[f] = dtc_share[f] * cax0[f], tcx_share[f] * cax0[f]
    opf[f]   = opfx[f] / (8760 * cf[f]);  cap0[f] = gen0[f] / cf[f]
    dlf[f]   = (1 - (1 / (1 + wacc[f])) ** life[f]) / (1 - 1 / (1 + wacc[f]))
for t in years:
    x = min(10, ln(gdppc[t-1 if t > base_year else t]))
    incf[t] = max(0, P4(x)) / 0.74 if IncElAdj starts with 'Yes' else 1
D = sum(bal[flow]['ecy'] for flow in demand_flows);  G = sum(gen0) * 8760 / 1000 / 11.63
gen_per_cons = G / D
sh_nxp = -(bal['imports']['ecy'] + bal['exports']['ecy']) / D
sh_tsd = -(bal['statdiff']['ecy'] + bal['transfer']['ecy'] + bal['distloss']['ecy']) / D
sh_eou = -bal['ownuse']['ecy'] / D
sh_add = gen_per_cons - 1 - sh_nxp - sh_tsd - sh_eou
```
:::

### Legacy power-input chains {#sec-pw-data-legacy}

The boxes below record, cell by cell, how legacy CPAT derives each power input (`CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb`,
cached run: Egypt, EGY, baseline). They are the specification from which the data step was rebuilt with formulas,
and they document legacy as it is, bugs included; the model departs from them in the five places listed above (L52-L56).
The items are every column of the former PowerTech table, every key of PowerPaths and of PowerParams.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: the legacy chains recomputed"}
Every copied cell was recomputed from the cached Mitigation values (the `v_Mitigation` dump) and compared with the
three tables: **0 mismatches** (relative tolerance 1e-12). This covers all 9 types × 17 traced type columns, all 37
path rows × 20 years, and all 22 parameters. When the data step was rebuilt with formulas, the Egypt values reproduced
legacy's cached values (macro series to 1e-15; power data to 1e-12), apart from the wind and solar capex time factors
for 2039-2041, where the model follows the Power tab cells legacy references (2041: legacy cached
solar 0.533 and wind 0.909; the Power tab 0.565 and 0.918).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Legacy chains: conventions of the legacy workbook"}
- **Year columns on Mitigation:** K = 2021, **L = 2022** (= `FirstYearCalculations`), M = 2023 … AE = 2041. Row 1
  holds the year headers (`L1 = FirstYearCalculations`, `K1 = L1-1`).
- **Type row order** in every engineer-model table: coa, nga, oil/oop, nuc, wnd, sol, hyd, ore, bio (row offset
  0..8). Tables A2, A4, A7 and A14/A15 use the code `oil` (column B); A16, B*, D* and later use `oop`. The Power and
  CoC tabs use `oil`.
- **Defined names:** the workbook-level names (sheet index −1 in `names.tsv`). The sheet-index-17 copies (sheet ECP)
  point one row higher in ScenarioDefinition (e.g. `CFOverrideIfAbove` → F376 instead of F377) and do not apply to
  Mitigation formulas. pyxlsb2 decoding confirms: `FirstYearCalculations` → `ScenarioDefinition!$F$232`.
- **ScenarioDefinition column F = Dashboard.** Every setting is
  `F<r> = IF($C$5, D<r>, IF($F$16="Default", IF(I<r>="Y", E<r>, G<r>), E<r>))` with `C5 = FALSE` ("MT is active")
  and `F16 = "Manual*"`, so F = E = a Dashboard cell (`E<r> = Dashboard!<cell>`).
- **XLOOKUP caveat in the `f_` dumps:** the LibreOffice conversion drops the first argument of every `_xlfn.XLOOKUP`
  (the dump shows `XLOOKUP(CoC!$B$202:$B$390,CoC!$D$202:$D$390,0.075)`; the true formula, decoded with pyxlsb2, is
  `XLOOKUP(G2988, CoC!$B$202:$B$390, CoC!$D$202:$D$390, 0.075)`). The WACC box gives the corrected formulas, which the
  cached values confirm.
- **Scenario index:** `Mitigation!C2173` = 1 in the baseline block (rows 2954-4300), from
  `INDEX($N$224:$AC$224, MATCH(B2173,$N$223:$AC$223,0))`. The carbon-tax copy sits at rows +6331 (from row 9285) with
  index > 1.
- **Country:** `_Countryname = ScenarioDefinition!F8 = Dashboard!E2` ("Egypt");
  `_Country_code = Dashboard!D644 = VLOOKUP(_Countryname, Countries!$C$6:$D$227, 2, FALSE)` ("EGY"). Formulas use
  `LOWER(_Country_code)` ("egy") for the Power codes; MATCH and XLOOKUP are case-insensitive.
- **Constants:** `_conv_ktoe_to_gwh = Mitigation!E1033 = 11.63` (typed); `_conv_gwh_to_mwy = E1044 = 1000/(365*24)`;
  `_conv_ktoe_to_mwy = E1034 = E1033*E1044 = 1.32762557…`; `_conv_kWh_to_GJ = E1045 = 0.0036`.
:::

- Tech adjustment table (X203:X211 × Y..AB = HIC/UMIC/LMIC/LIC), LMIC column AA: bio .03215 (row 203), nga .02465
  (204), coa .02465 (205), ore .04425 (206), hyd .02725 (207), sol .02935 (208), oil .02465 (209), nuc .02725 (210),
  wnd .02935 (211). `CoC!D253` (EGY) = 0.09947642998297449.

**The CoC tab (rows 200-390).** Title A200 ">>> Real WACC"; header row 201: A Country, B Country_Code, C S&P,
**D201:V201 = 2022..2040**, X201 "Tech Adjustment". Rows 202-390 (189 countries, alphabetical): A name, **B ISO3
upper-case (lookup key)**, C rating (or "Not Found"). D..V: real WACC by year (only D used; Egypt row **253**).
These are `LET` formulas (the WACC calculator): `rf + β·(ERP_US + CRP)` weighted by the equity share, plus
`(rf + default spread + lender margin)·(1−tax)·(1−equity share)`; rf = `XLOOKUP(year, A24:A34, C24:C34)` (real
risk-free rate); β, CRP, default spread, tax, equity weight, lender margin = `XLOOKUP(code, B41:B197, H/F/D/G/I/J41:197,
<row 172>)`; ERP_US = E192. Countries missing from the fixed data (65 rows, C = "Not Found") get **row 172 (Sri
Lanka)** through the if_not_found argument (e.g. AFG = LKA = 0.177883…; bug L56). From M (2031) the values repeat
the previous year. Tech adjustment table: X202 "(CPAT) Tech", Y202:AB202 = HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC; X203:X211 = bio, nga,
coa, ore, hyd, sol, oil, nuc, wnd; **Y203:AB211** typed additive premiums. Lookups: country
`XLOOKUP(LOWER(iso), CoC!$B$202:$B$390, CoC!$D$202:$D$390, 0.075)` (0.075 if missing); premium
`XLOOKUP(tech, CoC!$X$203:$X$211, XLOOKUP(income, CoC!$Y$202:$AB$202, CoC!$Y$203:$AB$211))`; Country* uses
`CoC!$Y$205:$AB$205` (coal row) for every type. Calculator inputs: rows 22-36 time data (A year, B nominal yield,
C real rf = `EXP(LN(1+B)−LN(1+$F$24))−1`, D US deflator, F24 = `(D31/D24)^(1/7)−1`); rows 40-197 fixed data (A
country, B code, C region/income, D default spread, E ERP, F CRP, G tax, H β, I equity weight, J lender margin; some
B/C/H/I cells are `=#N/A`).
:::

**`gen_per_cons` and the shares (base year L = 2022).**

- **L3741, total final power demand (ktoe):** `=SUM(L3725:L3739)`, `L37xx = E37xx`;
  `D3725:E3738 = TRANSPOSE(_Power_Use_Formatted)`, `_Power_Use_Formatted = Mitigation!G582:T583`; `E3739 = $V$583`;
  `G583..T583 = IF($C$578, E531..R531, …)`, `V583 = T531`; row 531 = Balances `ecy` (C503) for the flows in
  `E529:R529, T529`: road, rail, domesair, domesnav, resident, food_forest, services, mining_chemicals, ironstl,
  nonferrmet, machinery, cement, other_manufact, construc, plus ononspec. Excluded: U583 (fuel transformation / own
  use) and nonenuse. Egypt: 15495.7198104.
- **L3748, actual generation (ktoe):** `=L3751/_conv_ktoe_to_gwh`; `L3751 = L3754/_conv_gwh_to_mwy`;
  `L3754 = L3813 = SUM(L3804:L3812)`; `L3804+i = M(A4 row)` (gen0): Σ gen0 (MWy) × 8.76 / 11.63. Egypt:
  18922.8876526.
- `I3722 = (L3748 − L3741 − L3742 − L3743 − L3744)/L3741`, so `I3723 = L3748/L3741` exactly.
- With `BalancesOrConsumption` = "Consumption" (ScenarioDefinition F234 = Dashboard G136; Egypt "Balances") the
  shares come from `J3719:J3721 = $H$573:$H$575` instead.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Legacy chains: bugs and oddities"}
The model fixes the bugs (register codes in brackets) and keeps nothing of the oddities that affect numbers.

1. **A2 rows 2981-2985 (wnd, sol, hyd, ore, bio), columns P..T (L52):** the inverted ISERROR logic returns the world
   value; country efficiency, fixed and variable O&M, WACC and lifetime of these types are ignored. Egypt: solar fixed
   O&M 15 instead of the country 11.831, which changes `opf|sol`.
2. **A4 column N, installed capacity (L53):** the range `Power!$F$357:$Y$357` (2000-2019) does not contain 2022
   (column AB), so N = #N/A; actual capacity factors are never used, the study values are, and the CFOverride bounds
   are dead. With the fix, Egypt's actual capacity factors (legacy 456 data: gas 0.385, wind 0.436, solar 0.347,
   hydro 0.592) are used and base-year gas capacity is 52 GW instead of 35.
3. **Hydro investment start, H4067 (L54):** `IF($L$3827>50%, …)` tests a year header (2022 > 0.5), so hydro always
   starts in the first year (2022 instead of 2030). The model starts hydro in the base year only if its generation
   share is above 50% (Egypt: from 2030).
4. **Regional and country code shadowing (L55):** MATCH over `Power!A25:A356` finds the regional rows (42-109) first
   for `chn.mpp.*`, `jpn.mpp.*` and `kor.mpp.*`: for China, Japan and Korea, region data replace country data (18
   codes). The model looks up the country block.
5. **A7 country ctf code:** `iso.med.ctf.t` has a different segment order from `wld.ctf.med.t`, and there are no
   country or regional ctf rows, so the country branch is dead.
6. **D2 nuclear fuel:** `L3353 = K2727` is shifted one column (2022 takes the 2021 value); the value is the typed
   Mitigation!K710:AE710 = 0.004, not Power!G22. No numeric effect.
7. **A15 (tcx)** uses A14's helper `$K3110` instead of `$K3121` (same value). A15 is labelled "not used in the model
   at all".
8. **K5 planned-retirement probe:** `INDEX(Power!$D$1749:$BD$1878,$I3992,L3990)` is offset by one row and three
   columns from the data range `G1750:BD1878`; the flag J3991 uses `F1750:F1857` while the MATCH uses `D1750:D1878`.
   Harmless today.
9. **CoC (L56):** countries without fixed data silently get Sri Lanka's parameters (row 172) as the XLOOKUP
   if_not_found; countries absent from CoC rows 202-390 get 0.075 + the premium. The model gives every country
   without risk data the default WACC, flagged.
10. **WACC is time-invariant:** only CoC column D (2022) is used, although D:V hold 2022-2040 (kept in the model).
11. **"Country*" WACC option** applies the coal premium (CoC row 205) to every type (kept in the model).
12. **`early_max` (J3975 = 0.8) is typed**, not linked to `MaxCostBasedEarlyRetirement` (0.8 today); the label says
    "80%".
13. **Power!G23** `=ROUND(AVERAGE(#REF!),2)` is broken (unused).
14. **shock:** the IFERROR fallback in E478 is the text `"0%"`; the test `M479=FirstYearCalculations+1` is always
    true.
15. **incf:** the 2022 GDP per capita uses the current year (`L2429 = L2442/L2428`) while later years are lagged.
    Post-policy GDP `L2443 = K2442*(1+L2446)` rebases on the previous **pre-policy** level, so endogenous GDP changes
    do not accumulate (zero in the baseline).
16. **The Balances lookup ignores the year column:** one year per country only.
17. **A2 column N range** `Power!E$25:E$355`, while the other columns use `:356`. No effect.
:::

Notation: `iso` = LOWER(country code); `idxC(t)` = `IFERROR(MATCH(iso&".mpp."&t, Power!$A$25:$A$356,0), idxW(t))`;
`idxW(t)` = `MATCH("wld.mpp."&t, Power!$A$25:$A$356,0)`; `PC(col,t)` =
`IF(INDEX(Power!col$25:col$356,idxC)>0, INDEX(..,idxC), INDEX(..,idxW))`; `PW(col,t)` = `INDEX(Power!col$25:col$356,
idxW)`; `P*(col,t)` = PC for coa, nga, oil, nuc and PW for wnd, sol, hyd, ore, bio (legacy bug);
`BAL(flow,fuel)` = `INDEX(Balances!$A$13:$Z$4044, MATCH(ISO&flow, Balances!$A$13:$A$4044&Balances!$E$13:$E$4044,0),
MATCH(fuel, Balances!$A$13:$Z$13,0))`; D = total final power demand (ktoe) = Σ Balances `ecy` over road, rail,
domesair, domesnav, resident, food_forest, services, mining_chemicals, ironstl, nonferrmet, machinery, cement,
other_manufact, construc, ononspec.
